extracted.intended_audience: Florida state agencies and staff responsible for rulemaking; agency counsel; regulated persons and administrative law practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory requirements and standards under Florida Statute §120.54 governing how state executive-branch agencies must develop, notice, adopt, modify, and maintain administrative rules (including emergency, uniform, and federal-identical rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking mandatory and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking is not a matter of agency discretion. Each agency statement defined as a rule by s. 120.52 shall be adopted by the rulemaking procedure provided by this section as soon as feasible and practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking shall be presumed feasible unless the agency proves lack of sufficient time to acquire necessary knowledge/experience or related matters not sufficiently resolved. Rulemaking shall be presumed practicable to provide fair notice unless agency proves detail/precision unreasonable or matter too narrow for rulemaking outside adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative implementation timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an act of the Legislature requires implementation by agency rules, such rules shall be drafted and formally proposed as provided in this section within the times provided in s. 120.74(4) and (5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow statutory timing requirements for rules implementing legislative acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: No statutory-delay of application unless explicit
rubrics_metrics.description: No statutory provision shall be delayed in its implementation pending an agency’s adoption of implementing rules unless there is an express statutory provision prohibiting its application until the adoption of implementing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Least-costly alternative requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In adopting rules, agencies must, among alternative approaches and to the extent allowed by law, choose the alternative that does not impose regulatory costs that could be reduced by adoption of less costly alternatives that substantially accomplish statutory objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must consider alternatives and preference less-costly approaches consistent with law and objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: No inherent rulemaking authority or penalties without legislative grant
rubrics_metrics.description: No agency has inherent rulemaking authority, nor authority to establish penalties for violation of a rule unless the Legislature specifically provides that the penalty applies to rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on retroactivity and pre-effective rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may adopt rules prior to the effective date of the statute but rules may not be effective until the statute is effective. An agency may not adopt retroactive rules unless expressly authorized by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may prepare rules in advance but cannot make them retroactively effective without express statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-subject rule requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rule adopted shall contain only one subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicially noticed material and opportunity to examine
rubrics_metrics.description: In rulemaking proceedings an agency may recognize any material which may be judicially noticed and may provide materials so recognized be incorporated into the record. Before the record is completed, parties shall be provided a list of these materials and reasonable opportunity to examine them and offer written comments or rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule may incorporate material by reference but only as the material exists on the date the rule is adopted; changes in the material are not effective unless the rule is amended to incorporate the changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a rule incorporates another rule of the same agency by specific reference, subsequent amendments are automatically incorporated unless contrary intent. Rules after Dec 31, 2010 may not incorporate by reference unless the material is submitted in prescribed electronic format to the Department of State and full text available free by hyperlink, or if posting would violate federal copyright law, provide statement and locations for inspection. A rule may not be amended by reference only; amendments must set out the amended rule in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special incorporation-by-reference procedure for DEP/water management
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Department of Environmental Protection or water management district rule is incorporated by reference in another agency’s rule to implement part IV of chapter 373, subsequent amendments to the incorporated rule are not effective as to the incorporating rule unless the incorporating agency notifies committee and Department of State of intent to adopt amendments, publishes notice of intent in the FAR, files copy with Department of State, and follows objection procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes become effective as to the incorporating rule 20 days after publication and filing unless a substantially affected person files an objection within 14 days of notice publication; the agency may not adopt portions objected to; must publish notice of objection and agency response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of State rule-indexing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule published in the Florida Administrative Code must be indexed by the Department of State within 90 days after the rule is filed. The Department of State shall by rule establish procedures for indexing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation limits for initiating rule development
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency head may delegate the authority to initiate rule development under subsection (2); however, rulemaking responsibilities of an agency head under certain subparagraphs may not be delegated or transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific responsibilities identified in statute (e.g., subparagraph references) cannot be delegated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of rule development content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Except when the intended action is repeal, agencies shall provide notice of the development of proposed rules by publication in the Florida Administrative Register before providing notice of a proposed rule. The notice shall indicate the subject area, provide a short plain explanation of purpose and effect, cite specific legal authority, and include preliminary text of proposed rules if available or state how to promptly obtain copies without cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readable language drafting standard
rubrics_metrics.description: All rules should be drafted in readable language: avoid obscure words and unnecessarily long or complicated constructions; avoid unnecessary technical or specialized language that is understood only by members of particular trades or professions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public workshops for rule development
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may hold public workshops for rule development. An agency must hold workshops, including regional workshops, if requested in writing by any affected person, unless the agency head explains in writing why a workshop is unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The explanation is not final agency action; failure to provide explanation when required may be a material error. When held, persons responsible for preparing the proposed rule must be available to explain and respond. Workshops may be facilitated by a neutral third person; notice in FAR at least 14 days prior and must indicate subject area, agency contact, place, date, time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiated rulemaking considerations and processes
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may use negotiated rulemaking and should consider it when complex rules are being drafted or strong opposition anticipated. Consider assembling a balanced committee of interested persons willing to negotiate in good faith and using group consensus as basis for proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If used, publish notice of negotiated rulemaking in FAR listing representative groups invited; persons who believe interests not represented may apply within 30 days; meetings of negotiating committee must be noticed and open to the public and chaired by a neutral facilitator; agency's decisions about using negotiated rulemaking and selection of representatives are not agency action and do not affect rights to challenge proposed rules under s.120.56(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-adoption notice required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to adoption, amendment, or repeal (other than emergency rules), an agency shall give notice of its intended action setting forth a short plain explanation of purpose and effect; the full text of the proposed rule or amendment and a summary thereof; reference to grant of rulemaking authority and to statutes or laws being implemented or interpreted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must include summary of agency's statement of estimated regulatory costs if prepared; statement that persons wishing to provide information regarding that statement or a lower cost alternative must do so in writing within 21 days; statement whether proposed rule is expected to require legislative ratification; procedure for requesting a public hearing; and a reference to date/place where the rule development notice appeared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and availability timing for proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall be published in the Florida Administrative Register not less than 28 days prior to the intended action. The proposed rule shall be available for inspection and copying by the public at the time of publication of notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing and targeted notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall be mailed to all persons named in the proposed rule and to all persons who at least 14 days prior have made requests of the agency for advance notice of its proceedings. The agency shall give such other notice as prescribed by rule to particular classes of persons to whom the intended action is directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing materials with the committee prior to adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: The adopting agency shall file with the committee at least 21 days prior to the proposed adoption date a copy of each rule it proposes to adopt; a copy of any material incorporated by reference; a detailed written statement of facts and circumstances justifying the proposed rule; a copy of any statement of estimated regulatory costs prepared; and a statement of the extent to which the proposed rule relates to federal standards or rules, and the notice required by subparagraph (a)1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of estimated regulatory costs (SERC) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency is encouraged to prepare a SERC. However, an agency must prepare a SERC if the proposed rule will have an adverse impact on small business or is likely to directly or indirectly increase regulatory costs in excess of $200,000 in the aggregate in this state within 1 year after implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SERC requirements are tied to impact thresholds and small-business effects as provided by s.120.541.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration and mitigation for small businesses/counties/cities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall consider the impact of the rule on small businesses, small counties, and small cities. Whenever practicable, an agency shall tier its rules to reduce disproportionate impacts to avoid regulating small entities that do not contribute significantly to the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency may define small business/county/city differently if necessary. Methods to reduce impact to consider include: (I) less stringent compliance or reporting; (II) less stringent schedules/deadlines; (III) consolidating/simplifying compliance; (IV) establishing performance standards or best management practices; (V) exempting small entities from requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules ombudsman consultation and adoption of alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If agency determines proposed action will affect small businesses as defined by the agency, it shall send written notice of the rule to the rules ombudsman at least 28 days before the intended action. The agency shall adopt those regulatory alternatives offered by the rules ombudsman and provided within 21 days that are feasible and consistent with objectives and would reduce impact on small businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If agency does not adopt all alternatives, it must file a detailed written statement explaining reasons before adoption and send copy to ombudsman within 3 working days. Adoption period for filing rule may be extended when alternatives are offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearing rights and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If intended action concerns any rule other than procedure/practice, the agency shall, on request of any affected person received within 21 days after publication of notice, give affected persons an opportunity to present evidence and argument. The agency may schedule a public hearing and, if requested by any affected person, shall schedule one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a public hearing is held, staff must be available to explain proposal and respond. If agency head is a collegial body and hearings are requested, the board shall conduct at least one hearing itself and may not delegate without consent of requesters. Material submitted within 21 days after publication or between publication and end of final hearing shall be considered and made part of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to separate proceeding when rulemaking inadequate
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking proceedings shall be governed solely by the provisions of this section unless a person timely asserts substantial interests will be affected and demonstrates the proceeding does not provide adequate opportunity to protect those interests; the agency shall suspend rulemaking and convene a separate proceeding under ss. 120.569 and 120.57.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly situated persons may be requested to join; upon conclusion the rulemaking resumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification or withdrawal of proposed rules pre-adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: After final public hearing or after time for requesting a hearing expired, if rule has not changed or contains only technical changes, agency shall file notice to that effect with committee at least 7 days prior to filing rule for adoption. Any non-technical change must be supported by the record of public hearings, in response to written materials submitted within 21 days, or in response to a proposed objection by the committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When change is made other than technical, agency must provide notice of change by certified mail or actual delivery to any person requesting it no later than 21 days after the required notice. Agency shall file notice of change with committee with reasons and provide notice at least 21 days prior to filing for adoption; publish notice of change in FAR at least 21 days prior. Agency may withdraw rule after notice required by paragraph (a) and prior to adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on modification/withdrawal after adoption and before effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: After adoption and before the rule becomes effective, a rule may be modified or withdrawn only when: (a) committee objects; (b) a final nonappealable order entered in a rule challenge; (c) if rule requires ratification, when >90 days have passed since filing without ratification (may withdraw but not modify); or (d) when committee notifies agency that an objection is being considered, agency may modify to extend effective date by not more than 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must give notice of decision to withdraw/modify in next available issue where original notice published, notify persons described previously, and notify Dept of State if required to be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements for final adoption and public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: If agency required to publish rules in the Florida Administrative Code, upon approval of agency head shall file with Department of State three certified copies of the rule; one copy of any material incorporated by reference certified by the agency; a summary of the rule; a summary of any hearings held; and a detailed written statement of facts and circumstances justifying the rule. Agencies not required to publish in FAC shall file one certified copy in office of agency head and make rules open to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing constraints for filing rule for adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule may not be filed for adoption less than 28 days or more than 90 days after the notice required by paragraph (a), until 21 days after notice of change, until 14 days after the final public hearing, until 21 days after a SERC has been provided to persons who submitted a lower cost alternative, or until the administrative law judge has rendered a decision under s.120.56(2), whichever applies. Extensions to 45 or 60 days apply in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When notice of change or public hearing published prior to expiration, filing period is extended; petition for administrative determination extends filing period to 60 days after ALJ decision or until 60 days after judicial review. At filing, agency must certify compliance with timing and statutory requirements and that no administrative determination pending. Committee shall certify whether agency has responded in writing to all material and timely written comments or inquiries. Dept shall reject noncompliant rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to withdraw noncompliant or untimely rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rule has not been adopted within the time limits or not adopted in compliance with statutory requirements, the proposing agency shall withdraw the rule and give notice of its action in the next available issue of the FAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date upon filing and committee review tolling
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule shall be adopted on being filed with the Department of State and become effective 20 days after being filed, on a later date specified, on a date required by statute, or upon legislative ratification. Rules not required to be filed become effective when adopted by agency head or upon ratification. If the committee notifies agency that an objection is being considered, the agency may postpone adoption and the 90-day filing period is tolled until committee completes review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rule adoption standards
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency finds an immediate danger to public health, safety, or welfare requiring emergency action, it may adopt any rule necessitated by the immediate danger by any procedure which is fair under the circumstances if: (1) procedure provides at least procedural protection given by statutes/constitutions; (2) agency takes only action necessary to protect public interest; (3) agency publishes in writing specific facts and reasons for finding immediate danger and reasons for concluding procedure used is fair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of emergency rules, other than certain local educational units, including full text, shall be published in the first available FAR and provided to the committee along with any material incorporated by reference. Agency's findings of immediate danger, necessity, and procedural fairness are judicially reviewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and duration limits for emergency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An emergency rule shall not be effective for longer than 90 days and shall not be renewable, except when the agency has initiated rulemaking to adopt rules addressing the subject and either a challenge to the proposed rules has been filed and remains pending, or the proposed rules are awaiting ratification by the Legislature. Nothing prohibits adopting identical rules through regular procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to constitutional/statutory provisions, an emergency rule becomes effective immediately on filing or on a date less than 20 days thereafter if specified and necessary due to immediate danger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rules of procedure and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administration Commission shall adopt one or more sets of uniform rules of procedure; agencies must comply unless an exception is granted. Agencies may seek exceptions by petition; Administration Commission may approve exceptions to implement other statutes, conform to federal fund requirements, or permit receipt of tax benefits under federal law, or as required for efficient agency operation. Reasons for exceptions must be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies adopting exceptions shall publish a separate chapter in FAC delineating provisions of agency rules providing exceptions and specifying alternatives chosen; each chapter organized like uniform rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rules content highlights
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules shall include, but are not limited to: scheduling of public meetings/hearings/workshops; procedures for conducting meetings/hearings/workshops and taking evidence/testimony/argument in person and by communications media technology; rules for protests and bonds; petition and hearing filing requirements; requirements for requests for administrative hearings in enforcement actions; procedures for petitions for declaratory statements; agency organization and operations statement on agency website; procedures for variances and waivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications media technology evidence/testimony/argument must be afforded equal consideration regardless of method; notices must state how to attend and name locations where technology facilities available. Limiting points of access to places not normally open to public presumed to violate right of access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform petition filing content for administrative hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules for petitions for administrative hearings shall require the petition to include: (a) identification of petitioner including e-mail; (b) statement when/how petitioner received notice; (c) explanation how petitioner’s substantial interests are or will be affected; (d) statement of all material facts disputed or that there are no disputed facts; (e) statement of ultimate facts alleged including specific facts warranting reversal/modification; (f) statement of specific rules/statutes petitioner contends require reversal/modification and explanation how facts relate; (g) statement of relief sought, stating precisely action requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform respondent request-for-hearing content in enforcement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules for filing request for administrative hearing by a respondent in enforcement actions shall require: (a) name, address, e-mail, phone of requesting party and counsel or representative for service; (b) statement that respondent requests an administrative hearing and disputes material facts alleged (identifying disputed facts) or requests hearing and does not dispute material facts; (c) reference by file number to administrative complaint and date received. Agencies may provide an election-of-rights form calling for this information only and not imposing additional requirements unless authorized by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for petitions for declaratory statements and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules shall provide for filing and prompt disposition of petitions for declaratory statements and describe the contents of notices that must be published in the FAR under s.120.565, including any applicable time limit for filing petitions to intervene or petitions for administrative hearing by persons whose substantial interests may be affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency organization and operations statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules shall require each agency head to provide a description of the agency’s organization and general course of its operations, and the statement must be published on the agency’s website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of federal regulations as state rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In pursuance of state implementation/operation/enforcement of federal programs, an agency may adopt rules substantively identical to federal regulations, following specific procedures: publish notice of intent in FAR at least 21 days prior to filing; provide copy to committee at least 21 days prior to filing; consider written comments received within 14 days after notice; rule adopted upon filing with Department of State; substantive changes require republishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule becomes effective no earlier than effective date of federal regulation. A substantially affected person may file objection within 14 days after notice of intent; agency shall not proceed with objected portions unless deemed frivolous. If federal regulation is invalidated or changed, agency must publish repeal/adjustments within specified periods; rules adopted pursuant to this subsection should specifically reference the federal regulation when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to initiate rulemaking and agency response timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person regulated by an agency or having substantial interest may petition an agency to adopt, amend, or repeal a rule or to provide minimum public information required. The petition shall specify the proposed rule and action requested. Not later than 30 calendar days after filing a petition, the agency shall initiate rulemaking, comply with the requested action, or deny the petition with a written statement of reasons for denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special procedures for petitions directed to unadopted rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition is directed to an unadopted rule, the agency shall within 30 days initiate rulemaking or provide notice in FAR that the agency will hold a public hearing on the petition within 30 days after publication. Purpose of the hearing is to consider public comments on scope/application and whether public interest is served by application on case-by-case basis vs adoption by rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If agency does not initiate rulemaking within 30 days after the public hearing, it shall publish statement of reasons and changes and file it with the committee; the committee may forward copy to legislative oversight committees and may hold a hearing and recommend legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines after petition-initiated rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: If agency initiates rulemaking after the public hearing, the agency shall publish a notice of rule development within 30 days after the hearing and file a notice of proposed rule within 180 days after the notice of rule development unless, before the 180th day, the agency publishes a statement explaining reasons for not having filed. If rulemaking is initiated, the agency may not rely on the unadopted rule unless it publishes a statement explaining why rulemaking is not feasible or practicable until conclusion of the rulemaking proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking record compilation and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: In all rulemaking proceedings the agency shall compile a rulemaking record including copies of: all notices for proposed rule; any SERC; written summary of hearings; written comments and responses as required; all notices and findings under emergency rules; all materials filed by the agency with the committee; all materials filed with the Department of State; and all written inquiries from standing committees of the Legislature concerning the rule. Each agency shall retain the record as long as the rule is in effect; when rule no longer in effect record may be destroyed per records-retention schedule.
